To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mutations of residues in the ligand coordination loop of the blue copper protein, amicyanin, relax the constraints on copper coordination, and that these changes lead to a significant increase in the reduction potential and a decrease in pK(a) for the ligand histidine.
the outer sphere hydrogen bonds that constrain copper coordination in blue copper proteins can also be used to tune reduction potentials and pK(a) values of the ligands.
the hydrogen-bond networks in blue copper proteins, which constrain the geometry of copper(I), also tune the reduction potential and the pK(a)s of the ligand histidines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that protein structure plays in determining the reduction potential for blue copper proteins.
the structural basis of the reduction potentials of blue copper proteins and how the protein environment constrains and tunes the redox potentials of the copper site.
the role of the protein matrix in tuning the redox properties of copper in blue copper proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reduction potential of the blue copper site in amicyanin is determined by the hydrogen bonding network of the protein, which constrains both the geometry of the copper(II)/copper(I) pair and the pK(a)s of the ligands.

the hydrogen-bond network that constrains copper ligation in blue copper proteins is an important determinant of E(0) in the wild type and is a key factor in the ability of these proteins to function as electron-transfer proteins in vivo.
the hydrogen bonds of the hydrogen-bond network constrain the copper(II)-bound state of the protein to a structure with a low E(0) value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reduction potential for blue copper proteins depends on the hydrogen bond network that constrains the copper coordination geometry, and that this network also determines the pK(a)'s of ligand residues.
a change in hydrogen-bond network can tune both E(0) and pK(a).
hydrogen-bonded networks of the kind that constrain copper coordination in blue copper proteins are also capable of constraining pK(a) values of histidines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrogen-bond networks that constrain the ligands of copper(II) in these blue proteins also constrain the ligands for copper(I).

the outer sphere network that constrains copper in blue proteins is a major determinant of the E(0) of these proteins and that the network of hydrogen bonds can be relaxed by mutations that lead to a significant change in E(0).

hydrogen bonds can play a significant role in constraining the coordination geometry and oxidation state of a copper site, and that the resulting electronic properties of the site can be modulated by changing the hydrogen-bond network.
